skill: Compute an indefinite integral by separating a sum or difference, extracting constant factors, applying known power integrals, and recombining with one arbitrary constant.
learner_operation: Read the integrand, simplify a product or quotient when necessary, identify each term's coefficient and exponent, integrate each term (raise the exponent by one and divide by that new exponent), preserve signs and combine. Radio learners must distinguish the resulting primitive from near-miss primitives; a blank preceding +C requests only its nonconstant part.
reasoning_steps: For moderate q-49063 distribute sqrt(x) through (2+x) and rewrite as powers 1/2 and 3/2.
For moderate q-49059 divide each numerator term by x^2 to obtain x^3+7x^-2.
Apply sum and constant factor rules, then the power rule to each term, then simplify and include C (or leave it outside the provided blank).
response_contract: Observed standalone moderate questions q-49063 and q-49059 each have one radio field with five math choices and a complete worked solution. Three moderate f(x) questions have one blank and external +C, but lack the preceding definition of f(x). Preserve response form per recovered family and compare complete answer banks. Easy polynomial examples and canonical e-372 establish the backbone; context-dependent logarithm blanks are not standalone evidence for a new moderate logarithmic family.
difficulty: Moderate: one algebraic distribution or quotient simplification followed by two elementary power integrals; no substitution, integration by parts, or unresolved prior parts.
invariants: Indefinite integral, two-term linearity with constant factors, known powers, and a final primitive with arbitrary constant.
One necessary moderate algebraic rewrite; no exponent -1 in a power-rule-only family.
Every radio bank has exactly one mathematically correct primitive; worked steps must follow the displayed integrand.
Provide all information needed by a standalone item; repair malformed captured TeX without preserving capture artifacts.
permitted_variations: Coefficients, signs, term order, and modest integer exponents in quotients may vary while leaving two elementary power integrals.
In sqrt(x)(a+bx), both coefficients, signs and order can vary while preserving distribution and half-integer integration workload.
Correct choice position and distractor assignments can vary, with dependent answers and explanations recomputed.
Reconstructed f(x) blanks can state f explicitly using the function recovered from that source solution; A/B by themselves do not define a general family.
answer_roles: Which choice is the primitive must follow coefficients, signs and exponents rather than position or a fixed expression shape.
Either coefficient/sign can determine the corresponding term in the primitive. Fixing all signs positive needs an instructional justification; the sum rule explicitly covers plus and minus.
The denominator exponent and numerator exponents may vary within the same simplification workload rather than copying q-49059's exact x^4 and -1/x outcome.
